tldr: MemoryBank is a novel long-term memory mechanism for LLMs inspired by the Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve, enabling models to store, recall, and selectively forget memories while building user portraits for sustained personalized interactions.
contributions: Introduction of MemoryBank, a human-like long-term memory mechanism enabling LLMs to store, recall, update memory, and draw user portraits

Demonstration of practical applicability through SiliconFriend, an LLM-based AI companion tuned with 38k psychological conversations that can recall past memories, provide empathetic companionship, and understand user behaviors
Showing generalizability across (1) open-source and closed-source LLMs, (2) bilingual Chinese/English support, and (3) with and without the memory forgetting mechanism
methods: The authors propose MemoryBank, structured around three pillars: (1) a memory storage system that records detailed chronological conversations, hierarchical event summaries, and dynamically updated user personality profiles; (2) a memory retrieval mechanism using a dual-tower dense retrieval model (similar to DPR) with FAISS indexing, where conversations and summaries are encoded into vector representations for context-specific recall; (3) a memory updating mechanism inspired by the Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve, where memory strength S is initialized at 1 and increased by 1 upon recall while resetting elapsed time t, modeling exponential decay R = e^(-t/S). They also build SiliconFriend by parameter-efficient tuning (LoRA, rank 16, 3 epochs on A100 GPU) of ChatGLM and BELLE with 38k psychological dialogues, then integrate MemoryBank for long-term companionship.
results: Experiments used 15 virtual users with diverse personalities over 10 days of conversations, with 194 probing questions generated by ChatGPT. SiliconFriend demonstrated capabilities in memory recall, provision of empathetic companionship, and understanding of user portraits. The system was tested with ChatGPT (closed-source), ChatGLM (open-source, 6.2B parameters), and BELLE (open-source, 7B LLaMA-based). Bilingual support in Chinese and English was validated. Qualitative analysis with real-world user dialogs and quantitative analysis with simulated dialogs both supported the effectiveness of MemoryBank.
limitations: The memory updating model is described as 'exploratory and highly simplified,' noting that real-life memory processes are more complex and influenced by various factors. The forgetting curve varies across different people and types of information. The parameter-efficient tuning stage using LoRA was only conducted for open-source LLMs (ChatGLM and BELLE), not for closed-source models like ChatGPT.
